summary: Session 3 of 4 complete (golden corpus generation + normalization layer). Landed tests/AccessHarvester.Integration/Pipeline/GoldenNormalizer.cs with three entry points (NormalizeManifest, NormalizeUnresolvedItems, NormalizePerObjectIr) per Decision 4. Ran Pipeline.Default().Run(...) against both canonical fixtures (HomeHealthCare.accdb and NorthwindDevEdition.accdb). Drift survey across two consecutive runs confirmed Decision 4's narrow scope: only Database.ExportedAt actually drifts; HarvesterVersion + Database.FilePath added defensively (vary across commits/hosts); per-object IR is byte-stable across all 7 categories on both fixtures, so NormalizePerObjectIr stays a no-op. Built a one-shot tmp/build-golden-corpus/ tool (gitignored) that links the actual GoldenNormalizer.cs source and produces samples/GoldenOutput/<fixture>/{kb,ir,manifest.json,unresolved-items.json}. raw/ excluded per Decision 3. Confirmed idempotency: builder against second staging run produces byte-identical golden. Total corpus 17MB (HHC 175 files, NW 397 files) — within Decision 3's 15-20MB band, well under the 100MB stop-rule. Inspected output for surprises: no malformed IR, no missing fields; the empty manifest collections are intentional V1 per Session 2's spec (per-category threading is follow-on; rich data lives in ir/<Category>/). Cross-provider verification: R1 gpt-5-4 returned VERIFIED with 0 issues in a single round. All 1885 tests pass, 2 skipped (synthetic-DB fixtures absent). Routed cost ~$0.072. Session 4 (regression gate + closeout) remains.

reason.specifics: Routed analysis (gemini-pro): Session 4's primary task is authoring a well-defined integration test (CanonicalGoldenRegressionTests.cs), a less complex and more mechanical task than Session 3's exploratory corpus generation. Sonnet provides sufficient capability for this implementation-focused work at substantially lower cost than Opus. Cross-provider session-verification goes to gemini-pro per the rule-based pairing for Sonnet output.
